## Overview

How well a model predicts data it has never seen is called generalisation, and it is the
reason for fitting a model at all. A flexible model can fit its training stations
perfectly and still predict new sites worse than the average count. This section splits
the error on new sites into bias, variance and noise, and chooses a model's complexity
honestly, with a penalty and with cross-validation, on the same simulated survey as the
rest of the course.
